The runtime runs hosted commands as the user that started it, in its worktree, with the output of a non-terminal, in the admission lanes described below; a command still waiting for its slot when its `--timeout` passes is refused, not started, so the caller runs it standalone. A runtime also keeps, between commands, the output of the Git reads that are pure functions of object ids or of the commit HEAD named when they ran, keyed by that commit and the shallow state (256 MiB, least recently used first; not for a linked worktree): the second `review-check` of this repository took about 10 s against about 25 s standalone, with the same output. The runtime admits hosted commands in two lanes, each with its own slots and a bounded queue: `short` (`surface-check`, about 10 ms on this repository) and `heavy` (the other hosted commands; `roadmap-check <slug>` takes minutes here), 2 and 1 slots by default and queues of 16 and 4; `pose runtime start|serve` take `--short-slots`, `--heavy-slots`, `--short-queue`, `--heavy-queue` and `--memo-mib` (default 256). A short query is not queued behind a heavy check, and a command that finds every slot of its lane busy and the queue full is refused before it waits and runs standalone. `status` and the handshake carry, per lane, `<lane>_slots`, `_queue_limit`, `_queued`, `_running`, `_admitted`, `_refused`, `_wait_ms_total` and `_wait_ms_max` in `metrics`. A measurement of the runtime on a real repository, with its thresholds fixed before the numbers, is `POSE_RUNTIME_MEASURE=<file> go test ./internal/cli -run TestMeasureTheRuntimeOnTheRealRepository`; its report is under `.pose/reports/`.\n\n**Review rounds.** The rounds of a scope are its sealed bundles that a completed delegated review concluded on, in the order those runs ended; `pose review verify`, `pose delegate ls` and `pose insights` show the round. From round 2, the generated brief (template `review-brief/2`; runs briefed with `review-brief/1` still verify) carries a `Previous round` section built from the ledger: every open finding with the identifier it keeps across rounds (`R<round>-<id>`), its severity, disposition and location, the previous run and its draft digest. The reviewer's draft is the fenced code block whose info string is `pose-draft`: JSON with `schema` `pose.review.draft/v1`, `decision` and `findings` (`id`, `severity` high|medium|low, `disposition` blocker|follow-up, `file`, `line`, `summary`), and from round 2 `prior_findings` (`id`, `status` fixed|partial|not-fixed|superseded, `evidence`) and `sweep`. A finding reported `partial` or `not-fixed` keeps its identifier in the next brief. A round-2-or-later draft that leaves an open finding unaccounted, calls one `fixed` without evidence or states no sweep is recorded with `draft_problems`, `wait` reports it as `invalid`, and it is never accepted as an approval. With `routing.rounds` `continue-thread` (the default) a round resumes the session the previous round ended with, through the agent's resume command; it opens a new session, recording why, when the agent or its vendor changes, the chain of drafts is broken, that session cannot be resumed, or the round reaches `routing.round_threshold` (5 by default), where `verify` also warns that the rounds are not converging. `cold-session` opens a new session every round. Each run records its `round` and `thread`; `pose insights` reports, per scope, findings per round, rounds to approval, and how prior findings were accounted for in continued and in cold rounds. A previous round whose record is not intact makes the brief refuse.

**decision: approved**

All three round-1 blockers are fixed. I found no high or medium defects in this round. What's left is low-severity, and each item is a follow-up with an owner and a review date.

## Previous findings
- **R1-F1: fixed.** `runtime_cmd.go:249-251` adds `metrics` to `status --json`, and `:266-273` prints it as `runtime.metrics.*`. `runtime_host_test.go:266-278` checks both outputs. The run-2 JSON report has a filled `runtime_metrics` (line 172).
- **R1-F2: fixed.** POSE.md:949 and locales/pt-BR/POSE.md:944 now say "in the admission lanes described below". A search of all four POSE.md copies no longer finds "one hosted command at a time".
- **R1-F3: fixed.** Report `.md:53` gives the effective figures: heavy lane 7 admitted, short lane 20 admitted, 0 refused, 0 ms wait. These match the counts the harness produces (1+5+1 heavy, 10+10 short).
- **R1-F4: partial.** The comment at `runtime_host.go:78` was updated, but `runtime_host.go:97` still says "One hosted command at a time". The concurrency proof is still only `surface-check --help` (`runtime_host_test.go:251`). It is recorded as a follow-up in spec line 131.
- **R1-F5: not-fixed.** `runtime_host.go:128,139,146` still reports `memo_hits` as the change in a counter shared by the whole process. It is accepted as a follow-up in spec line 131.
- **R1-F6: fixed.** `runtime_measure_test.go:186-201` compares the short query with standalone, both idle and under load.
- **R1-F7: fixed.** `runtime_measure_test.go:217-238` reads VmHWM after the concurrent phase.

## New findings (all low, follow-up)
- **N1** `pose-mcp/internal/cli/runtime_cmd.go:128`: the usage text still lists only `--idle`, `--drain` and `--json`. It leaves out the five new admission flags.
- **N2** `pose-mcp/internal/cli/runtime_lanes.go:23`: when GOMAXPROCS < 2, the default short-lane slots quietly drop to 1. R6 and POSE.md:949 say the default is 2.
- **N3** `pose-mcp/internal/cli/runtime_measure_test.go:196`: the heavy `review-check` that runs alongside the short queries throws away its `via` and its output. The T5 verdict text (line 267) still says every hosted run matched standalone.
- **N4** `pose-mcp/internal/cli/runtime_cmd.go:175`: `restart` starts `serve` again with default admission settings, so any non-default settings from the earlier `start` are lost. Separately, `status`, `stop` and `attach` accept the admission flags and silently ignore them. Neither behaviour is documented.
- **N5** `pose-mcp/internal/cli/runtime_cmd.go:78-89`: nothing tests the error path for bad values (`--heavy-slots 0`, a value that isn't a number, a missing value).

## Criteria
- **Thresholds T1–T6:** identical in the spec (R8), the test constants (`runtime_measure_test.go:32-37`) and both report runs. All six passed.
- **Classification:** `shortCommands` contains only `surface-check`, which matches D1 and the timings stated in the spec.
- **Known gaps:** the simultaneous-arrival gap is stated honestly. The check at `runtime_lanes.go:58` (queue full *and* every slot busy) is the cause, and Go's channel handoff keeps the window small.
- **Refusal leads to standalone:** a lane-full refusal comes back as `OutcomeRefused`, and `runtime_host.go:209-210` then runs the command standalone.
- **Plan tools:** I ran `artifact-check --strict` (only orphan warnings for files outside this change) and `surface-check --strict` (0 findings).
